audit_method: Manual inspection of public GitHub repository metadata, pinned README/source-catalog text, license declarations, and source-manifest references. This is a discovery/candidate register, not legal sign-off.

audited_catalogs.notes: The source catalog explicitly says each row retains its original dataset license and that code MIT does not relicense the corpus. Good discovery index. Do not import the benchmark rows into training.

Catalog contains per-dataset license fields and attribution guidance. It mixes explicit CC0/CC-BY/OGL with inferred US federal public-domain classification. README says 2,239 unlicensed datasets quarantined while export-manifest says 2,994; discrepancy unresolved. Repository metadata reports no repository-level license. Never bulk-admit from its allowlist; inspect each underlying record, publisher terms, and payload.

HPLT release pages label corpus packages CC0 and report enormous Spanish/Catalan volumes, but the source material is from Common Crawl/Internet Archive crawls. The CC0 packaging statement is not treated as proof that each crawled third-party text is rights-cleared. Do not ingest until source-level provenance and reuse basis are available.

integration_decision.reason: Manual source audit is not a substitute for per-version rights proof, immutable payload hashes, privacy/quality checks, deduplication, split integrity, and global G-0. Eulogikon metadata is separate from underlying text; CC0 scope is limited to Eulogikon's preparation layer/manifests. Added CoVoST CC0 translation-only lane and OpenAlex CC0 bibliographic-metadata lane; neither is admitted pending immutable source versions, hashes and applicable quality/privacy gates. Added bounded CoVoST 2 translation-field-only and OpenAlex anonymous-S3 metadata-only acquisition adapters. Both export candidate artifacts and proposed rights records; neither appends the rights ledger or enables training. Successful candidate workflows generated 432,274 unique CoVoST translation rows (86,751,966 bytes) and 100,000 OpenAlex metadata rows (259,309,375 bytes). Both rights candidates passed the registry validator and were appended as two exact-scope level-A rights records; neither dataset is admitted or training-eligible. Candidate-only acquisition counters are tracked separately from admitted counters: two candidate payloads were downloaded and two exact-scope rights records were validated, while admitted payloads, admitted level-A records and training-eligible records remain zero. Added ScienceVerse Collabra and Hlido as further pinned candidates pending their own item-level/hash/privacy checks. Expanded discovery register with VoxPopuli ASR transcript-only, DReaM-es-open, HTRogène Occitan, and DFKI SmartData German NER/relation corpus. These remain candidate-only pending exact payload manifests, source-level rights, hashes and privacy/quality checks. Expanded discovery with ROR v2 (CC0 metadata, GeoNames location fields removed), MathemAct (CC-BY but quarantined for user-generated content/privacy), Common Corpus (per-document license filter required), HPLT (CC0 claim but crawl-origin rights unresolved), Gutenberg (per-work/per-edition public-domain checks), ScienceVerse, Hlido, Correlation Studio, and explicit quarantine/exclusion decisions for Perseus CC-BY-SA and two UD treebanks with mixed/conflicting source-text rights. Added United Nations Parallel Corpus v1.0 (six-language public-domain claim, exact archive/jurisdiction review pending), BNE digital-library catalogue/OCR metadata (CC-BY-4.0 metadata; per-work OCR rights required), and COCOTEROS Spanish contextual-generation corpus (CC-BY-4.0, exact Zenodo payload audit pending). HPLT was explicitly quarantined because a CC0 package label does not establish rights in all crawled source texts. Added ParlaIbero-ES v2.0 (562,514 Spanish parliamentary rows, CC-BY-4.0, Dataverse ZIP ~1.01 GB), CorpusNÓS/Nos_Corpus_Periodistico Galician journalism (159,986 documents / 55.9M tokens, but per-publisher rights required), and GovEasy Spanish administrative procedures (438 records, CC-BY-4.0, snapshot and source attribution pending). Corrected HPLT classification: CC0 covers packaging only, not underlying text, so text ingestion is excluded pending item-level rights. Common Corpus records per-document license variability and PII observed in legal-document examples; strict filtering required. Added direct Wikidata structured-data CC0, World Bank CC-BY default with dataset-level exception checks, and Eurostat statistical reuse as a policy-compatibility candidate. Added a bounded Common Corpus streaming filter adapter; it rejects non-allowlisted per-document license labels, excludes OpenGovernment and screens basic email/phone patterns, but keeps outputs in a human review queue only. Added anonymous Dataverse metadata preflight for ParlaIbero-ES v2.0; it resolves exact file IDs, declared sizes, provider checksums and restriction flags before any 1 GB payload is downloaded. ParlaIbero-ES v2.0 preflight succeeded: 17 unrestricted files / 1,059,811,627 declared bytes, with 1,058,266,687-byte ES_interventions.csv pinned by Dataverse file ID 14215089 and provider MD5. Only the metadata manifest artifact was acquired; the 1.06 GB speech payload remains undownloaded pending review. Added three independently documented CC0 discovery lanes: DBLP bibliographic metadata, Wikidata structured namespaces only, and Mozilla Common Voice release data (pending exact release datasheet, access and privacy review). Added Dryad (per-dataset CC0), Europeana (metadata-only CC0), Smithsonian (item-level CC0 marker only), Open Library (catalog metadata only), NASA mission data (file-by-file CC0 only), and NIST PDR (per-record license required). Three bounded candidate ingestions have completed and their hashes/artifact IDs are now recorded: CoVoST 432,475 translation rows (86,874,752 bytes), OpenAlex 100,000 bibliographic records (185,943,561 bytes), and ROR 144,717 metadata records (87,981,707 bytes). These are candidate outputs only, not admitted training data. Added NASA NTRS as per-document rights discovery only, and explicitly excluded OpenStax (CC BY-NC-SA) and The Stack v2 (bulk access requires agreement; mixed repo licenses and sensitive data risks). Verified additional exact candidate artifacts: CoVoST run 41932647180 / artifact 13372451541 (432,475 translation rows; 86,874,752-byte payload; SHA-256 fc7f70d7ca75c2eef50a710b579186332d3082f5aa4369ee01039aab6d8ff58e); OpenAlex run 41932684850 / artifact 13371129725 (100,000 metadata rows; 185,943,561-byte payload; SHA-256 a167fac571d5c172f531bd5c2ddb35c9ca06506919522ac187e602c3b9599cf8); ROR run 41933051951 / artifact 13370819701 (144,717 valid JSONL metadata records; 87,836,990-byte payload; SHA-256 f4ec624eeb6ff4fe3015525dd8b0327c1610af3edd029d25862672ec75d7158c). Exact Level A rights records for these three latest payload versions were appended after hash, source-scope and validator review; rights registry now contains five exact-scope records, with run 41933238345 passing. Common Corpus run 41932708586 / artifact 13372806543 scanned 11,738 rows, accepted 3,000 candidate rows (1,243 CC0, 3 CC-BY-3.0, 2 CC-BY-4.0, 1,752 MIT), rejected 8,233 license labels, 470 privacy-pattern rows and 11 malformed/oversized rows. MIT code rows are now excluded in the follow-up run until per-repository notice bundles are preserved; all Common Corpus outputs remain review-only. Added Crossref bibliographic metadata (CC0, abstracts excluded), DataCite DOI metadata (CC0, public API), and OpenCitations Index/Meta (CC0 data; site/API documentation has separate licenses). Crossref/DataCite bounded public API adapters are now in the repository; they exclude article abstracts, descriptions, full-text and PDF links. Additional metadata-only CC0 acquisitions completed: Crossref run 41933591839 / artifact 13373310817 exported 1,000 bibliographic records (679,289 bytes; SHA-256 a3a19cb17378e8d6e68d8263f9207a786106beddd82ffa0a95916f8cbf75d4a0); DataCite public API in the same run exported 1,000 dataset DOI records (6,786,926 bytes; SHA-256 5d514bda3c9452e6f0042f05c4aab37ec5aa291bbb71f17896bf31b7c80058e9). Both excluded abstracts/descriptions and content payloads; candidate rights records passed validation and were appended to the exact-scope rights ledger. Ledger now contains seven Level A records; admitted/training-eligible counts remain zero. Common Corpus follow-up run 41933173350 / artifact 13373006118 exported 2,159 candidates after removing MIT rows (2,149 CC0, 4 CC-BY-3.0, 6 CC-BY-4.0; 5,971,320 bytes); 17,472 non-allowlisted license rows, 311 privacy-pattern rows and 8 invalid/oversized rows were rejected. The subsequent corrected artifact run 41933372089 / artifact 13371639293 confirms valid JSON/JSONL review-queue files; Common Corpus remains unadmitted. Crossref and DataCite adapter run 41933591839 succeeded: 1,000 Crossref rows (679,289 bytes; SHA-256 a3a19cb17378e8d6e68d8263f9207a786106beddd82ffa0a95916f8cbf75d4a0) and 1,000 DataCite dataset DOI metadata rows (6,786,926 bytes; SHA-256 5d514bda3c9452e6f0042f05c4aab37ec5aa291bbb71f17896bf31b7c80058e9). Both exact-scope Level A rights records were appended and validated; ledger total is seven. Added a bounded OpenCitations Index adapter with no token/credentials, 30-request cap and public rate-limit pacing; its first smoke run is pending. OpenCitations Index run 41933797143 / artifact 13372309071 completed without credentials: 20 DOI queries, 24 citation rows, zero request failures, 9,431-byte JSONL payload, SHA-256 75269b5f18a464e5b872c611ab4bfb50687dc679c36d61f37f8a3cdf0f442ff6. The exact-scope CC0 metadata rights record passed validation and was appended; rights ledger now contains eight Level A records. None is admitted/training-eligible. Added a second CoVoST lane for bilingual source sentence + target translation text. The upstream README's CoVoST-data CC0 declaration covers the data fields; the adapter exports only sentence/translation and excludes audio, paths, client IDs, Tatoeba and code. This preserves the previous translation-only artifact and produces a separately hashed bilingual candidate. CoVoST bilingual-pair preflight was deliberately withdrawn: official CoVoST README confirms the source sentence comes from the separate Common Voice v4 validated.tsv, while the CoVoST translation TSV supplies the translation/path/split. The separate Common Voice v4 file has not been acquired or independently rights-verified without credentials, so no sentence/translation merge was performed; the failed exploratory adapter and workflow were removed. The translation-only CC0 candidate remains intact. Added a no-credential DReaM-es-open Korp API preflight. It checks corpus metadata and 100 sample hits only; if Korp requires BasicAuth it fails closed and no credentials are supplied. Full corpus export remains pending source and bulk-access review. GovEasy static candidate adapter was tested against dataset.jsonld, /en and /ca but the publisher host returned HTTP 404 in GitHub Actions; no files or rights records were downloaded. Automatic retries were disabled to avoid noisy failures; source remains a discovery candidate pending host recovery. Source-specific cautions: COCOTEROS is now quarantined at field level because its paper says source sentences originate in Tatoeba (per-item CC BY 2.0-FR/varied licenses), even though the derived dataset declares CC BY 4.0; no text payload is admitted. DReaM-es-open public Korp API works without credentials and reports 9,115,151 tokens / 717,854 sentences, but its first deterministic sample included English Google Books boilerplate and a Zapotec grammar document; language and underlying work rights must be filtered per document. Added GPLSI ClearText CAS v1.0 and ClearText VAL v1.0 as pinned Spanish/Valencian easy-read candidates. BOE-A-2025-12053 lists both UA-GPLSI corpora as CC BY 4.0, but the adapter quarantines explicit NC/ND source notices and retains per-document source metadata; no blanket relicense of third-party source texts is assumed. DReaM-es-open metadata index was inspected: 128 document records, 114 authors, 94 described languages, 9,115,151 tokens and 717,854 sentences. The corpus is a historical grammar/documentation collection, not homogeneous Spanish prose. Public Korp API preflight works without credentials, but no text has been bulk-exported; author/edition/source rights and text language must be verified per document. Added ten SINAI-UJA source records: Emoti-SP (tiny Apache-2.0/BOE CC BY 4.0 dual-license candidate), iSOL and CRiSOL (Hugging Face CC BY-NC-SA conflicts with BOE CC BY claim; excluded), COAH TripAdvisor reviews (quarantined for third-party platform rights/privacy), MentalRiskES (excluded sensitive health data), and five ALIA corpora/hard-negatives declared CC BY-SA 4.0 (excluded by current allowlist). This prevents permissive-looking BOE declarations from overriding more specific dataset-card licenses and privacy risks. GPLSI ClearText workflow 41935114828 / artifact 13373282757 succeeded. CAS: 11 candidate documents, 1 quarantined NC-ND source document, 907,806-byte JSONL payload SHA-256 e7cc5b66aa50dc2ba296ffeb348ea0f4e9a3c10fe22de93860bfe6fd0c1945cd. VAL: 6 candidate documents, 0 quarantined, 221,948-byte JSONL payload SHA-256 15ea1a2495f312ee95e213cc4d851f9e3dca7c7d1e5c13259f3c859479a8219d. All 17 candidate JSONL records and review queue were parsed; 1 explicit CC BY-NC-ND document was quarantined. These remain item-level rights review only, with no Level A record and no training admission.
